chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from 'Ammar ibn Musa, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him):

Concerning a man who forgets to wash his posterior with water until he has prayed, having wiped with three stones: He said: 'If it is still within the time of that prayer, he must repeat the wudu and repeat the prayer. If the time of that prayer has already passed, then his prayer has been valid, and he should perform wudu for the prayers ahead.'
And concerning a man from whom wind exits — is he required to perform istinja? He said: 'No.'

And he said: 'When a man urinates and nothing other than urine exits from him, he need only wash his urethra alone and not wash his posterior. And if something exits from his posterior and he has not urinated, then he need only wash the posterior alone and not wash the urethra.'
And he said: 'He need only wash what is external/visible of it, and it is not incumbent upon him to wash its interior.'

And he was asked about a man who performs wudu then touches the inner part of his posterior. He said: 'His wudu is nullified. And if he touches the inner part of his urethra, he must repeat the wudu. If he is in prayer, he stops the prayer, makes wudu, and repeats the prayer. And if he exposes/opens his urethra, he repeats the wudu and repeats the prayer.'

What the beginning of this hadith contains regarding the command to repeat wudu and prayer when one has wiped with three stones as long as one is within the prayer time — this is to be interpreted as a recommendation (mustahabb), because istinja with stones is permissible, as we have explained.

key_terms.اَلاِسْتِحْبَابِ: istihbab — the fiqh status of a recommended (mustahabb) act
key_terms.اَلاِسْتِنْجَاءَ: istinja — ritual cleansing of private parts after answering nature's call

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rule for a man who forgot to use water for istinja after wiping with three stones and then prayed?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), via 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, delivers several rulings on istinja: forgetting water after using three stones before prayer (repeat wudu and prayer if within prayer time; otherwise valid); no istinja required for passing wind; each discharge requires washing only its respective organ; touching inner parts of posterior or urethra nullifies wudu. Shaykh al-Tusi's appended note clarifies the first command to repeat is recommended (mustahabb), not obligatory, since istinja with stones is valid.
